title: One question, and only when the turn needs it
body: Both product voices cap the question. Galion One: one question, and only when you need it to continue. Do not interview them. Galion Research: the one question that would change the answer, asked after what you can already say. Do not open with a questionnaire. R3 makes ask-one a legal move at most once in a turn. On Galion One it is legal only when the turn cannot continue without it. On Galion Research it is the question that would change the answer. A second question in the same turn fails the compile. This is how the product avoids turning curiosity into an imposition. It is not a claim that Brown and Levinson's negative-face calculus was applied, because that book was not re-opened.
